source.citation: Ogden FL et al. (2015), A new general 1-D vadose zone flow solution method, Water Resources Research 51:4282-4300

source_bound_state_topology.bin_occupancy: binary at a given depth: a bin is locally full or empty
water_types: water connected simultaneously to land surface and groundwater or an indefinitely deep initial condition
source_bound_state_topology.infiltration_front_state: front depth z_j per active bin
source_bound_state_topology.groundwater_front_state: capillary-rise height H_j per active groundwater-connected bin relative to water table
source_bound_state_topology.falling_slug_state: detached water interval whose top and bottom advance together under the source assumption of balanced capillary forces
source_bound_state_topology.capillary_relaxation: post-advance internal redistribution/sorting across bins; source states it conserves mass when implemented correctly
source_bound_state_topology.falling_slug_groundwater_merge: slug water that reaches a groundwater front is merged into that front and raises its capillary extent by the transferred amount

source_bound_groundwater_semantics.constant_head_lower_boundary: groundwater fronts advance or retreat per bin by taking water from or giving water to the groundwater table
source_bound_groundwater_semantics.dynamic_water_table: source uses a predictor-corrector step that adjusts groundwater-table motion for vadose-zone uptake/release and is described as mass conservative
source_bound_groundwater_semantics.coupling_claim_in_source: coupling to a 2-D groundwater solver is described as a straightforward non-iterative predictor-corrector
source_bound_groundwater_semantics.SWAP5_limit: the source does not by itself establish the exact SWAP5 H_SWAP=H_MF and q_SWAP=-q_MF residual contract, arbitrary coupling-window semantics or a response tangent

source_bound_numerical_work.higher_order_note: source cites fourth-order Runge-Kutta allowing infiltration timesteps of order 60 s in prior analysis

state_bound_assessment.reason: The publication describes detached falling slugs produced by forcing hiatuses, but the inspected article text does not prove a hard maximum number of simultaneously disconnected slug intervals per bin over arbitrary forcing history.
state_bound_assessment.required_proof: derive from source code/data structures and event rules whether each bin has a fixed finite number of front/slug coordinates or whether repeated detach/reattach events can accumulate multiple disconnected intervals

SWAP5_interface_implications.theta_profile: can be reconstructed from bin occupancy/front geometry but is not stored on a fixed depth grid by the native method
SWAP5_interface_implications.head_profile: requires constitutive inversion and a defined projection from front/bin geometry onto requested process depths
SWAP5_interface_implications.root_uptake: source removes water from the least tightly bound available bins within root zone; SWAP5 must instead qualify a solver-neutral conservative sink mapping that preserves SWAP process semantics
SWAP5_interface_implications.drainage_and_macropore_exchange: finite-volume source/sink insertion is structurally possible, but process-specific transfer ownership and depth mapping remain unqualified
SWAP5_interface_implications.oxygen_stress_and_solute_transport: need stable depth-based hydraulic views; front internals must remain hidden
SWAP5_interface_implications.groundwater: scientifically promising; exact MODFLOW interface residual/tangent still open

critical_interpretation: FWC has stronger native groundwater and source/sink semantics than a simple infiltration approximation, but this does not remove the main SWAP5 risk: a theta-domain front representation must provide bounded state and cheap, sufficiently accurate depth-profile hydraulic views to every other SWAP process. That interface cost may be as important as the front ODE cost itself.
